bib.title: From RAGs to rich parameters: Probing how language models utilize external knowledge over parametric information for factual queries

question: When a language model answers a factual query with retrieved context in the prompt, how much does it use its parametric memory versus the context?
hypothesis: Implied: with RAG context present, models rely on the context and minimally on parametric memory (a 'shortcut').
contributions: First study using three mechanistic probing methods (causal tracing, attention contribution, attention knockout) on RAG vs vanilla factual recall
Finding that MLP parametric memory is minimally used when context is present
Finding that the last-token residual stream draws on the attribute token in context rather than the query subject token

method.summary: Runs causal tracing, attention contribution and attention knockout on Llama-2 7B and Phi-2 2.7B for factual queries from the Knowns Fact dataset, in a vanilla setting (query only) and a RAG setting where GPT-4-generated context holding the answer once is prepended. Compares MLP indirect effect and subject-token versus attribute-token influence on the last token.
method.task: mechanistic interpretability of factual recall with RAG context

datasets.name: Knowns Fact Dataset
datasets.split: all 1209 for attention contribution; random 50 prompts for causal tracing

datasets.name: Synthetic RAG contexts (GPT-4)
datasets.size: one context of five 20-word segments per query
datasets.source: generated by GPT-4 from Knowns queries; attribute appears in exactly one of five segments (placed in first segment per footnote 1) and the query text in none
datasets.preprocessing: regenerated until a check passed (attribute occurs exactly once, query string absent)

other.variant: not stated whether base or chat

inference.samples: causal tracing on 50 random prompts; attention contribution on all 1209; runs/seeds not stated
inference.prompting: RAG prompt: 'Information is below:' + five segments + 'Given the context information and not prior knowledge, complete the following:' + query; vanilla is the query alone
inference.retrieval: no real retriever; synthetic GPT-4 context. A Wikipedia RAG pipeline was tried and dropped for lack of control

parameters.causal_tracing_noise: spherical Gaussian, mean 0, std 3 sigma (sigma = std of sample of token embeddings), Meng et al. default
parameters.rag_corruption: in RAG runs the whole context plus subject is corrupted; in vanilla only the subject
parameters.attention_contribution_selection: top 5% of subject-to-last-token contributions plotted; 70% of layers contribute ~0
parameters.knockout: attention weights between positions set to -inf at a layer, all heads

other.causal_tracing_time: 4-5 hours for 20 word segments of 5 count (footnote 2)

metrics.name: Average Indirect Effect (AIE)
metrics.definition: mean over prompts of probability of answer in corrupted-with-restoration run minus corrupted run, per hidden state

metrics.name: Attention contribution norm
metrics.definition: norm of attention contribution from a token (subject or attribute) to the last token, summed over heads (SAT-Probe, Yuksekgonul et al.)

metrics.name: Probability drop under attention knockout
metrics.definition: percent decrease in probability of predicted token when attention from a token to last token is blocked

baselines: vanilla (no context) setting for each model
eval.protocol: descriptive comparison; no significance tests, seeds or intervals reported

limits: Short, synthetic, well-formed context with the answer exactly once; real retrieval is noisy and depends on retriever, ranker and hyperparameters (authors).
Long context not studied: causal tracing cost is prohibitive; position, proximity and recency bias left for future work.
Instruction-tuned and RLHF models not examined; only Phi-2 2.7B and Llama-2 7B.
Causal tracing on only 50 prompts; no seeds, intervals or significance tests.
Prompt tells the model to use 'the context information and not prior knowledge', which may drive the shortcut; no condition without that instruction.
Only factual completion of the form (s, r, o); Fig 3 caption ratios (twice, 5 times) disagree with the text numbers.
Attention contribution plots use only the top 5% of contributions, chosen 'to amplify the difference'.
